why_used: The theoretical result that portfolio weight constraints act as a form of shrinkage, so constraining a portfolio substitutes for estimating its covariance matrix more accurately. title: The Devil Is in the Details: The Risks Often Ignored in Low-Volatility Investing
identifier: The Journal of Portfolio Management 46(7) 58-70; DOI 10.3905/jpm.2020.1.163
why_used: Counter-evidence that must be engaged rather than omitted. Reports that optimiser-based low-volatility construction is highly sensitive to risk-model inputs, affecting sector and stock positioning and risk exposures. The study finds a 25 basis point spread in realised volatility across four estimators, so the manuscript reconciles the two: the sensitivity shows up in positioning, which the concentration and sector-tilt tables measure, while a binding sector band and turnover cap absorb it before it reaches realised risk.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher.
retrieval_notes: Via DOI. Metadata confirmed against Crossref.
